what_it_does:
microsoft/TokenEconomizer (pinned d58755d, Apache-2.0) is a hook-driven cost-control plugin for coding agents. It runs on Claude Code, Codex and Copilot CLI, with Pi, opencode and Cursor (experimental) as well. It learns from a repository's finished sessions and uses three mechanisms to cut repeated cost in later sessions.
(1) micro-skills: short repository facts, such as the working test command, injected at SessionStart. Default off.
(2) toolprune: denies tools, Codex capability packages or Copilot MCP servers that a repository's sessions never used. It writes them into the host's own project settings. Default auto.
(3) loopguard: inside a turn, detects a failing loop. A judge model (a side call through the user's own agent CLI) decides, then the guard injects a redirect and finally a notice telling the person how to stop the turn. It never stops the turn itself. Default nudge.
An optional repomap (default off) injects aider's tree-sitter/PageRank symbol map, cut to a token budget. It is not an embedding, vector store or knowledge graph.
A ledger prices every session and the plugin's own model calls in cache-weighted effective tokens.
It is a token and cost layer, not a data map. It cannot replace OAW's LLM wiki and does not address the user's graphify/vectorization wish. Its README headline numbers (18.4–30.9% lower cost on SWE-bench, Pass@1 up in 4 of 5 combinations and −1.0 for Claude Code + Opus 4.8) are the paper's claims. I did not verify them.
mechanism:
Components and how data moves, checked against the source, not just the README:

ENTRY
- Claude Code plugin: plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json declares commands ./slash-commands/. plugin/hooks/hooks.json registers "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/te-hook" on six events with no matcher: SessionStart (timeout 15s), UserPromptSubmit (20s), PostToolUse (60s), PostToolUseFailure (60s), Stop (10s) and SessionEnd (10s) (hooks.json:4-69).
- Codex plugin: plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json:19-20 declares hooks ./hooks/codex-hooks.json and skills ./codex-skills. Codex has five events (no PostToolUseFailure), plus a commandWindows variant that runs `python -c` with runpy on te_bootstrap.py.
- te-hook is a POSIX sh script. It picks TE_PYTHON, python3, python or py (skipping the WindowsApps stub), sets PYTHONUTF8=1 and execs te_bootstrap.py hook.
- te_bootstrap.py sets umask 077 and TE_PLUGIN_ROOT. It then locates the package in this order: $TE_CORE_PATH, <plugin>/lib (a git symlink), the symlink-stub target, the plugin's parent, then the clone recorded in ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json or the `source` in ~/.codex/config.toml (te_bootstrap.py:57-118). It does sys.path.insert(0, core) (line 156) and calls tokeneconomizer.plugin.hook.main.
- hook.main reads JSON from stdin. It does nothing when TE_SIDECALL=1 or TE_DISABLE=1 (hook.py:67), turns any exception into `{}` plus a line in errors.log, and redirects stray stdout to stderr.

CONTROLLER (controller.py)
- SessionStart:
  - rewrites the ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te launcher (line 96)
  - injects the cached micro-skill block if that mechanism is on
  - emits toolprune notices
  - checks whether side calls are paused
  - may spawn a repomap refresh
  - pins the session to a repository and may spawn `te repos migrate`
  - spawns a detached `te fold` for any earlier session that was not folded (lines 93-174)
- UserPromptSubmit: opens a loop-guard turn and, when repomap=on, adds a map ranked against the prompt.
- PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure: folds the call into TurnGuard. Once the repository has a learned "envelope" (5 turns that ended green), a free gate decides when to start a detached judge job (judge.py, AsyncJudge). The verdict, with its model-written redirect, is picked up on a later call and injected as context, at most loopguard_nudges=1 times per turn. After that only a notice is given; on Claude Code the model is asked to relay that notice word for word (hosts.py:160-166).
- Stop: closes the turn; a turn that ended green feeds the envelope.
- SessionEnd: spawns a detached `te fold`.

BACKGROUND
- context.spawn starts `python -m tokeneconomizer.plugin.cli ...` detached (start_new_session on POSIX, context.py:73-93).
- On Windows, winspawn.py first tries CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB. If that fails, it calls PowerShell Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process.Create, with the command and the full environment written to a spec JSON in the state dir (winspawn.py:44-66).
- Detached jobs: fold, judge, repomap refresh, repos migrate, and `toolprune apply-pending`. The last one is a waiter that loops for up to 24h, polling every 600s (fold.py:51-52, cli.py:355-375).

FOLD (fold.py)
- Parses the host transcript through trace/ (claude, codex, copilot, pi, opencode, cursor readers).
- Runs PrefixStage (micro-skills) and ToolingStage (toolprune evidence).
- Micro-skills:
  - The envfacts layer works with no model.
  - The distiller makes one paid proposer call every k=3 sessions. That call reads digests of the last 8 sessions (command templates, edited basenames, masked error lines; raw blobs capped at 20k/40k characters) and authors facts with regex detectors plus regex-only extractors. No eval or exec anywhere.
  - Lifecycle (lifecycle.py:14-21): promotion after K=3 confirmations on tasks that edited different files; decay γ=0.8; contradiction weight λ=5; a high-stakes fact is retired on one contradiction; a fact is injected only if it fired on at least 40% of at least 4 exercised tasks.
  - The rendered block is capped at max_facts=4 and max_tokens=150 (config.py:149-150).
- Toolprune: a never-used tool, capability or server is proposed after at least 10 unused prompts over at least 2 sessions, or after 5 sessions (fold.py:97-107; tripled for high-risk tools). Under `auto` it is held until the repository has been idle for 60 minutes (or at most 24h) so a warm prompt cache is not invalidated, then written by denylist.apply. Claude Code: permissions.deny in .claude/settings.local.json. Codex: marked toggles in .codex/config.toml, applied only in trusted projects. Copilot: disabledMcpServers in .github/copilot/settings.local.json. A file the plugin creates is added to .git/info/exclude. A symlink leading out of the repository and unparseable JSON are refused (denylist.py:111-170). Protected tool sets include Bash, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Agent, Task, Skill, ToolSearch, WebFetch and WebSearch (adapter.py:37-50).

SIDE CALLS (sidecall.py)
- Claude: `claude -p --output-format json --max-turns 1 --tools "" --strict-mcp-config` (empty config), `--model haiku`, `--no-session-persistence`, run in a temp dir (lines 202-235).
- Codex: `codex exec --json --disable hooks --ephemeral -s read-only` (lines 238-245); each call carries Codex's ~25k-token base prompt.
- Copilot: `copilot -p` with every tool denied and MCP servers disabled.
- All use TE_SIDECALL=1. Usage is priced into ledger.jsonl (accounting.py, pricing.py: per-model-id weights, input 1 / cache_read 0.1 / cache_write 1.25 / output 5 for Claude; an unknown model id fails hard).

STORAGE
- Everything lives under $TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME or ~/.tokeneconomizer (paths.py:26-30): repos/<slug-sha1(remote or path)>/<host>/ holding injection.json, untool.json, envelope, sessions/*.json, events.jsonl, ledger.jsonl, plus judge/, manual_state/, bin/te, errors.log and config.json.
- No database, no vector index.
- The repository key is the normalized origin remote, so clones and worktrees share state (paths.py:188-249).

CLI
- `te` offers status, microskills, toolprune show/apply/restore/refresh-catalog/measure, config, repos, doctor, fold and probe.
- `measure`, `refresh-catalog` and `probe` make explicit model or catalog probes: claude -p init events, `codex debug prompt-input` (free), and a 127.0.0.1 HTTP capture server for Copilot (toolcheck.py:144).

hosts.claude_code: Native plugin installed from its own marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json, source ./plugin). hooks/hooks.json is loaded by Claude Code's plugin convention (plugin.json does not name it) and registers six events with no matcher through the POSIX sh launcher te-hook, which runs Python 3.10+. There are 7 slash commands and no SKILL.md for Claude. Toolprune writes permissions.deny to the project's .claude/settings.local.json. The README claims support for 2.1.300–2.1.310 (not verified here; OAW's pilot used 2.1.309, inside that range). On Windows it relies on Git Bash for the sh launcher. CI runs on ubuntu and windows with Python 3.10 and 3.13 (tests.yml).
hosts.codex: Native Codex plugin (.codex-plugin/plugin.json): hooks ./hooks/codex-hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd; commandWindows uses python -c with runpy) and 5 codex-skills SKILL.md (status, config, repos, microskills, toolprune). The user must choose 'Trust all' for hooks, and they take effect from the next session. Codex below 0.141 runs no plugin hooks; the README says 0.153.1–0.164.0. Toolprune writes marked toggles into the project's .codex/config.toml (trusted projects only), including the 'collaboration' package: features.multi_agent=false and agents.enabled=false. Its toolprune skill tells the model to request sandbox_permissions=require_escalated for apply/restore. Side calls go through `codex exec -s read-only --ephemeral`.
hosts.other: Copilot CLI: copilot-hooks.json plus .github/plugin/plugin.json; prunes whole MCP servers through .github/copilot/settings.local.json. Pi: TypeScript extension (package.json pi.extensions). opencode: TypeScript plugin, experimental. Cursor Agent: experimental, macOS/Linux only, built with scripts/build_plugin.py. There is no MCP server anywhere.

runtime_requirements: Python >=3.10 on PATH (python3, python or the Windows py launcher; TE_PYTHON overrides). The core package uses only the standard library: pyproject.toml:18 dependencies = [].
POSIX sh for the plugin/scripts/te and te-hook launchers. On Windows that means Git Bash for Claude Code; Codex on Windows uses the commandWindows python -c variant.

The host agent CLI signed in (claude, codex, copilot, pi, opencode or cursor-agent). Paid side calls bill the user's plan or account: the loopguard judge and nudge writer by default, the micro-skills proposer when enabled. The Claude default is haiku. Codex calls carry about 25k base-prompt tokens each.
git binary (subprocess: rev-parse in repomap, ls-files in denylist), plus direct reads of .git/config.
Detached background processes: te fold, te judge, te repomap refresh, te repos migrate, and the te toolprune apply-pending waiter (up to 24h, polling every 600s).
Windows only: PowerShell plus WMI Invoke-CimMethod Win32_Process.Create as the fallback for spawning detached processes; pythonw.
Optional: aider-chat (pyproject extra 'baselines') in any Python, only for repomap, which is off by default. pytest only for tests.
Node/TypeScript runtime only for the Pi and opencode extensions.
Persistent local state in ~/.tokeneconomizer or $TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME (JSON/JSONL files; no database, no vector store).
No network services. A 127.0.0.1 ThreadingHTTPServer runs only during explicit Copilot probe and measure commands.

gates.evidence: LICENSE lines 1-3: 'Apache License Version 2.0, January 2004'. plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json:10 and .codex-plugin/plugin.json declare "license": "Apache-2.0". There is no NOTICE file, so only LICENSE retention and marking of modified files apply.

The Codex SKILL.md files are small. Names: status, config, repos, microskills, toolprune. Descriptions are 226–303 characters and bodies 529–1482 bytes, far under 24000 B (measured with tools_te_digest/fm.py). But this is a hook plugin, not a skill package: Claude gets slash-commands with no SKILL.md, and the value sits in tokeneconomizer/ (about 13k lines of Python). The repo also contains a git symlink (`git ls-files -s`: 120000 ... plugin/lib/tokeneconomizer -> ../../tokeneconomizer). The OAW ingest gate rejects symlinks (skill-catalog-execution.md:74).

Seven issues:
1. Hooks on 6 events with no matcher (plugin/hooks/hooks.json:4-69).
2. Default toolprune=auto writes host permission config without a per-change prompt (config.py:152; fold.py:312-341; denylist.py:52-54).
3. Windows job-object escape through CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB, falling back to WMI Win32_Process.Create, which writes the full process env to a spec JSON (winspawn.py:27,44-66).
4. The Codex skill tells the model to request sandbox_permissions "require_escalated" (plugin/codex-skills/toolprune/SKILL.md:17).
5. Model-written redirects and relay instructions are injected into the agent's context (controller.py:329-355; hosts.py:160-166).
6. Hook code is loaded from the mutable clone path through known_marketplaces.json or the Codex config.toml `source` (te_bootstrap.py:57-118,156).
7. Model-authored regexes are compiled (distiller.py:346-362; ReDoS-only risk, no eval or exec found).
Mitigations: umask 077, refusal of symlinks that leave the repo (denylist.py:111-121), user-written deny entries never touched, fail-open hooks, TE_SIDECALL recursion guard, side calls with `--tools ""` and `-s read-only`.

No telemetry, update check or HTTP client in tokeneconomizer/ or plugin/. Grep found only urllib.parse (cli.py:748) and a 127.0.0.1 capture server for explicit Copilot probes (toolcheck.py:144-160). However, default-on loopguard (config.py:158) makes paid model calls through the user's agent CLI: sidecall.py:217-223 runs `claude -p ... --model haiku`, and sidecall.py:238-245 runs `codex exec`. These send session digests to the provider (docs/PLUGIN.md:548-552).

Home directory: ~/.tokeneconomizer holds state, ledger.jsonl, events.jsonl and errors.log (paths.py:26-30), plus a bin/te launcher rewritten at every SessionStart (paths.py:53-84; controller.py:96), and winspawn spec JSON files with the environment (winspawn.py:56-60). In the project, toolprune writes host configuration: .claude/settings.local.json permissions.deny, .codex/config.toml, .github/copilot/settings.local.json and .git/info/exclude (denylist.py:52-54,141-170). Reads: ~/.claude/plugins/known_marketplaces.json and ~/.codex/config.toml (te_bootstrap.py:57-95); ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (cli.py:510-520); host transcripts under ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.copilot.

pyproject.toml:18 `dependencies = []`. The optional extras are test (pytest) and baselines (aider-chat>=0.60, pyproject.toml:45), used only by repomap (off by default, config.py:162) in a separate process (repomap.py:8-12). Python >=3.10 matches OAW.

Partly redundant.
Claude Code already defers MCP tools through ToolSearch; TE's own trace/claude.py:157 says deferred tools 'cost one listing line each... matter little to the bill'. Prompt caching already discounts re-sent tool schemas (pricing.py:1-12 acknowledges this). Users can set permissions.deny or --disallowedTools themselves. Native CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and auto-memory cover hand-recorded repo facts like micro-skills.
Not redundant: the loopguard (in-turn stuck judge plus redirect) and transcript-learned pruning have no native equivalent that I could confirm.
Net savings on top of native features in OAW's hosts are unknown until measured.

Micro-skills overlaps oaw-evidence/context_hub (project facts) but works the opposite way: automatic and push-based versus explicit, pull-based recall (context_hub.py:386-399, max_chars 512–1e6, default 12000). The TE ledger overlaps the improvement.py METRICS ('tokens','latency_ms','cost_usd', improvement.py:22). Toolprune, loopguard and repomap have no OAW slot. TE's loopguard nudge also resembles the 'mandatory nudge' explicitly excluded in v2.0.0-execution.md:78.

Ships both Claude Code (plugin/hooks/hooks.json plus slash-commands) and Codex (plugin/.codex-plugin/plugin.json:19-20 hooks plus codex-skills), with a Windows Codex variant (codex-hooks.json commandWindows). Mechanism coverage differs: Claude prunes single tools, Codex prunes capability packages (README.md:310-317).

Always-on metadata is small: 5 Codex skill descriptions, about 1290 characters (~320 tokens), and 7 Claude slash-command descriptions, about 670 characters (~170 tokens), measured with fm.py. By default nothing is injected at SessionStart, since micro-skills is off (config.py:148). When enabled, the block is capped at ≤4 facts/≤150 tokens (config.py:149-150). Repomap adds 2048 tokens when on (config.py:163). Caveat: OAW core and pack budget numbers are not defined yet (P5), and mid-turn redirect and relay injections are not counted here.

Codex skill names are generic: 'status', 'config', 'repos' (plugin/codex-skills/*/SKILL.md frontmatter), namespaced as tokeneconomizer:. The 'status' description ('Use when the user asks about TokenEconomizer, its status...') sits next to OAW's planned oaw-status skill for progress questions (skill-catalog-execution.md:323). No trigger test exists. The Claude side is manual slash commands, so risk there is low.

Hard conflicts with OAW policy for bundling:
- Skill_Guide.md:17 says 'OAW does not silently edit `.claude` settings', but TE's default auto toolprune writes permissions.deny (config.py:152; denylist.py:52).
- v2.0.0-execution.md:78 says 'Do not add a second model runtime ... background self-rewriting daemon' and excludes 'mandatory nudge'; TE has side-call runtime, detached waiter and loopguard nudges.
- skill-catalog-execution.md:313 says the packaging allowlist must 'reject hooks and auto-approve permissions'; TE is hook-driven.
- Skill_Guide.md:40 says 'usage diagnostics stay with the host'.
- README.md:142 says 'Evidence, not instructions', but TE injects model-written redirects and an instruction to repeat notices word for word (hosts.py:160-166).
- Concrete clash: Codex toolprune 'collaboration' sets features.multi_agent=false and agents.enabled=false (denylist.py:61-64). OAW-bundled EGM needs subagent sessions (skill-catalog-execution.md:275).

oaw_overlap:
There is no single OAW component it maps to, and no capability slot it could fill cleanly:

(1) Micro-skills vs oaw-evidence/context_hub. Both supply project facts. OAW's are human-recorded and pulled on demand, with citations and a hard bound (memory recall --max-chars, default 12000; search --compact). TE's are learned automatically from transcripts and pushed at SessionStart (≤4 facts/≤150 tokens). OAW v2 explicitly removed automatic memory and telemetry loops (v2.0.0-execution.md:86), so the automatic part conflicts. TE's fact lifecycle (confirm, decay, contradict, firing gate) is a useful heuristic for marking OAW evidence superseded.

(2) TE ledger/pricing vs scripts/improvement.py. improvement.py compares operator-reported raw 'tokens', 'latency_ms' and 'cost_usd'; any assertion regression rejects, a 5% saving makes a result eligible, and a resource increase over 10% rejects. TE's cache-weighted effective tokens (per-model-id price ratios, hard fail on unknown ids) and its rule that the harness's own model calls count against the arm are more rigorous definitions of those same metrics. TE's own headline (Pass@1 −1.0 with 30.9% cheaper for Opus 4.8) would be 'rejected' under OAW's no-quality-regression rule.

(3) toolprune measure vs the catalog's context-budget ('撐爆上下文') gate. The plan currently estimates startup metadata tokens. TE shows how to measure real request size: `codex debug prompt-input` is free; on Claude, two haiku `claude -p` calls with and without a `--settings` change.

(4) Loopguard and repomap: OAW has nothing comparable. OAW's wiki_sync renders docs/raw into docs/knowledge and is not a code-symbol map. Neither TE feature is a vector or knowledge map that could replace the LLM wiki.

(5) Shadow mode resembles OAW's preview-before-apply (`migrate` without --apply), but applied to measuring a mechanism.
integration_rationale:
Absorb its methods; do not pack or bundle the tool itself.

The plan's order of preference puts absorbing methods first. Packing requires that OAW lacks the capability AND that integration is clean. Integration is not clean:
- TE is a hook-driven runtime. The packaging allowlist rejects hooks and auto-approved permissions.
- By default it writes the host's permission and configuration files.
- It runs detached background processes (fold, judge, a waiter of up to 24h) and makes paid side calls through nested agent CLIs. OAW v2 forbids a second model runtime and background daemons, and promises not to silently edit .claude settings.
- On Codex it can concretely regress OAW's own bundled EGM: after about 5 sessions without subagent use, auto toolprune writes features.multi_agent=false into the project's .codex/config.toml, which counts as 'diarrhea'.

It does satisfy the cross-host rule (Claude plus Codex) and the license and stdlib-dependency gates. The paper's savings are not proven against native ToolSearch deferral and caching in OAW's host versions.

The valuable parts are measurement and lifecycle methods, and they fit existing OAW parts without adding a skill:
- cache-weighted effective tokens and overhead charging, in improvement.py and the acceptance protocol
- real prompt-size probes, in the catalog context-budget gate
- shadow (log-only) arms, in oaw-improve
- prompt-cache-aware timing (apply only between sessions)
- bounded-injection caps and fact confirmation/contradiction counters, as advisory metadata in oaw-evidence and wiki_sync freshness checks

Absorbing measurement methods changes no model-facing behavior, so it needs no paid A/B; it only needs fixture tests in harness_check.

If a user still wants TE itself, it stays the user's choice through its official marketplace install. OAW would record the pinned SHA and the evidence, recommend toolprune=propose or shadow, and set loopguard per the A/B results. It would never be installed by OAW. Any claim that TE plus OAW saves cost, and any future move to pack status, depends on the paid A/Bs listed (that path is needs_ab_first).
nutrients: improvement.py metrics: define 'tokens' as cache-weighted effective tokens. Weights come from the billed model id: Claude input 1, cache_read 0.10, cache_write 1.25, output 5. Fail hard on an unknown model id instead of silently mispricing (pricing.py:1-30, accounting.py:17-26). Record raw totals alongside.

Overhead charging: every model call the harness or candidate makes (judges, graders, proposers, sidecalls) goes into the same ledger as the arm it serves, and overhead_frac is reported (accounting.py:33-47, ledger.py). This puts into practice SHARED_ACCEPTANCE_PROTOCOL's rule that totals cannot be claimed without child usage.

Catalog context-budget gate: measure startup cost instead of estimating it. On Codex, `codex debug prompt-input` with and without the candidate (free, no model call). On Claude, `claude -p 'Reply with exactly: OK' --output-format json --model haiku --max-turns 1 --no-session-persistence` with and without --plugin-dir/--settings, summing input + cache_read + cache_creation. A failed probe is an error, never 0, because 0 would read as 'all saved' (toolcheck.py:216-249). Whether Codex skill metadata appears in prompt-input still needs checking.

Shadow mode: a candidate computes and logs every decision without acting on it (config.py:26-28; controller.py `if not self.cfg.shadow`). Use it as a free pre-A/B arm in oaw-improve and in the catalog's behavior-digestion step, to measure how often a skill would fire before spending A/B budget.

Prompt-cache-aware timing: apply changes that alter the startup prefix (skill installs, AGENTS.md edits, tool sets) only between sessions or after a cache-TTL idle window, because a resumed conversation would otherwise rewrite its whole cache (fold.py:41-49; toolprune_quiet_minutes=60). Add this as guidance for OAW migrate --apply and catalog absorb.

Evidence lifecycle heuristics, as advisory metadata only, for oaw-evidence and wiki_sync freshness lint: promote after 3 confirmations on independent tasks; recency decay γ=0.8; contradictions weigh λ=5× a confirmation; a high-stakes note is retired on one clean contradiction; surface a note only if it was relevant in at least 40% of at least 4 exercised tasks (lifecycle.py:14-21). Notes stay human-recorded and pull-based.
Hard caps on any always-on injected block (≤4 items, ≤150 tokens; config.py:149-150), as a rule for any future OAW SessionStart or AGENTS.md growth, matching OAW's bounded recall.

Cheap nested evaluation calls for OAW's EGM pilot graders: run headless `claude -p` with `--tools ""`, `--strict-mcp-config` plus an empty `--mcp-config`, `--no-session-persistence`, a temp cwd, and an env marker so the user's plugins and hooks do not recurse. TE measured about 570k vs 14k effective tokens for a one-line call with and without 31 MCP servers attached (sidecall.py:202-223); that is the authors' measurement, not verified here.

README animation technique for OAW's planned metabolism animation: an animated teaser generated reproducibly from a script (docs/assets/teaser.py), with a static fallback through <picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)">. Whether GitHub honors that media query is unknown; OAW's plan already prefers a pure SVG+CSS animation.
diarrhea_risks: Breaks bundled EGM on Codex. After ≥5 sessions, or ≥10 prompts over ≥2 sessions, with no subagent use, auto toolprune writes `features.multi_agent=false`, `agents.enabled=false` and `include_collaboration_mode_instructions=false` into the project's .codex/config.toml (denylist.py:61-64,72; fold.py:97-107,254-258; config.py:152). EGM skills are manually invoked and need subagents, so a repository where EGM simply wasn't used for a while loses it.

Silent edits to host permission settings: default auto writes permissions.deny into .claude/settings.local.json and adds it to .git/info/exclude. This contradicts OAW's 'does not silently edit .claude settings' promise, and `oaw.py doctor` cannot see it. Rarely used MCP tools needed by explicitly invoked skills can be denied.

Latency on every tool call: PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure have no matcher (timeout 60s), so each tool call starts sh plus Python plus package imports plus state I/O. This pollutes OAW's latency_ms metric (10% maximum_resource_regression) and EGM A/B timing, especially on Windows.

Unmatched A/B arms: mid-turn redirects written by a model and injected into context, plus 'repeat this notice word for word' relays (hosts.py:160-166). They conflict with 'Evidence, not instructions' and can change outcomes in OAW behavior tests.

Background daemons and a second model runtime: detached fold, judge, repomap and migrate jobs, plus an apply-pending waiter that lives up to 24h (fold.py:51-52; cli.py:355-375). On Windows these escape the host's job object through WMI and write the environment to a spec file (winspawn.py:44-66).

Unexpected billing: the loopguard judge is on by default and uses the user's quota. Each Codex side call carries about 25k base-prompt tokens (sidecall.py:14-17). OAW's 'no automatic spend' boundary would be crossed.

Duplicate fact sources if micro-skills is turned on: auto-learned facts from repository-controlled command output (an injection surface, PLUGIN.md:553-558) compete with oaw-evidence, and an agent can get conflicting 'how to run tests' guidance.
Unpinned code: hooks load the package from the live clone path (te_bootstrap.py:57-118), so a `git pull` changes running hook code without any OAW SHA or hash check.
Codex prompt fatigue: the toolprune skill asks for require_escalated sandbox approval, and installation needs 'Trust all' for hooks.
Trigger collision: generic Codex skill names ('status', 'config') next to OAW's planned oaw-status progress skill.
proposed_ab_tests: A1. Four-arm stream A/B on Claude Code 2.1.309 and current Codex: A native, B native+TE (defaults), C native+OAW default (EGM + evidence), D native+OAW+TE. Use a fixed fixture repository with a test trap (bare pytest fails, python -m pytest/unittest works, as in TE's probe.py) and run ≥8 sequential sessions per arm, because TE needs history (envelope e=5, toolprune s=5). Repeat ≥5 times. Measure: per-scenario×assertion pass counts; cache-weighted effective tokens including TE overhead; wall time; hook latency p50/p95 per tool call; number of TE judge and side calls. Gate: D ≥ C (parity) with no assertion regression; claim 'improvement' only if D > C.

A2. EGM regression under TE on Codex: seed or run 5 sessions without EGM so TE applies the 'collaboration' deny, then run EGM's 30 test_scenarios plus the seeded-defect design set.
